title: IMPECCABLE: A Digital Twin Drug Discovery Workflow Comprising AI, Physics and Experiment & the Creation of Nanomolar-Potent Inhibitors
summary: Overnight measurements at lower altitude predicted acute mountain sickness diagnosed at 4554 m in the study cohort. Five-fold cross-validation in 20 participants; no independent or prospective external validation; small-sample and feature-selection limitations.

source_review.scope: PMC full text Methods/Results reports K-nearest-neighbor classification from overnight pulse-oximetry features in 20 lowlanders after staged ascent; the model predicts clinically established acute mountain sickness at 4554 m, with 100% accuracy for the specified 2600 m feature set under five-fold cross-validation. The primary record dates publication 2026-09-30; no earlier version was located in checked primary records. Exact DOI/title comparison against active and archived snapshots found no match. Caveats: very small cohort, exploratory design, internal cross-validation only, and potential feature-selection leakage noted in the analysis.
